findings.required_action: Before final minimal-statement admission, try to discharge these constructor-facing witnesses internally. If retained, describe them honestly as redundant source solution conditions, not indispensable stochastic assumptions. Do not substitute a new continuity hypothesis.
findings.text: Joint measurability hX,hY is explicitly part of the natural source but mathematically follows here from strong progressivity: restrict to countably many integer horizons, weaken each filtration sigma-algebra to the ambient one, and glue the measurable restrictions. No direct global named lemma was found in the inspected Adapted API.

findings.proposed_source_clarification: Add to the natural conclusion: G, extended constantly to negative times, is continuous and locally integrable; the balance also holds for any a,b>=0 with the oriented integral convention.
findings.text: The candidate exposes Continuous G and LocallyIntegrable G for the clamped real extension and allows all nonnegative a,b in the oriented integral. Source P6 justifies continuity, and F1 extends from a<=b by antisymmetry; these are valid derived strengthenings.

hypothesis_necessity_summary.normalization: N>0 is the source convention for a genuine particle average. The totalized Lean inverse and empty sum might make a degenerate N=0 identity vacuously true; no such extension is claimed.
hypothesis_necessity_summary.usual_conditions: Used by the existing actual stochastic-integral producer. This review does not claim they are the mathematically weakest possible construction hypotheses.

phase: Source/statement acceptance before proof construction and elaboration

proof_topology_and_api_coverage.assessment: Use finite product compactness and joint continuity to bound full-configuration coefficients on each [0,T]. Compose progressive configuration processes and invoke bounded_measurable_coefficient_along_progressive_process; sphereMeasurableNoiseIntegrand gives exact noise representatives. Derive initial coordinate measurability from strong progressivity.

For each particle use Euclidean state index Fin 2 x Fin d, driver Fin d and polynomial squared difference. Identify the internally constructed coordinate process with the supplied pair on the horizon event, and its compact range with the image of sphere x sphere. Derive any fallback element required by the compact-Ito API from supplied states; do not add a dimension-positivity or nonempty-state premise.

For r=||x-y||^2 and u=<x,y> on the unit sphere, r=2(1-u) and ||P_x-P_y||_F^2=2(1-u^2)=2r-r^2/2. Thus the radial drift plus shared-noise Hessian term is -2*lambda*(d-3)*r-lambda*r^2. The last expectation is exactly E||delta||^4. The single-state sum of squared projection columns alone is insufficient: prove the difference/cross term.

The compact-Ito producer yields the actual derivative martingale and M(0)=0. Derive integrability and zero expectation from that martingale before using weak_integral_balance_of_centered_increment or an equivalent direct Fubini argument. Finite sums create no cross-particle quadratic covariations. Derive balances from zero to each horizon and subtract; do not assume cross-horizon equality of separately constructed integral representatives without proof.

Recover continuous paths on each horizon from the coordinate equations and existing integral continuity, then use countably many horizons for a global event. Since bX,bY depend on all particles, expected-generator continuity must use the full C x C state and its compact marginal law, or a direct dominated-continuity proof. A per-particle-pair marginal cannot encode the displayed generator without extra dependence restrictions. Apply FTC on positive times and within Ici 0 at zero.

recursive_binder_and_definition_audit.compiler_limit: Only the unelaborated candidate and the actual current public definitions were reviewed. No compiled type, implicit-instance printout or proof term exists for this candidate yet.
recursive_binder_and_definition_audit.drift_and_time_measure: prefixIntegralProcess b t omega is the integral of b over TimeMeasure.upTo t. TimeMeasure.upTo is the NNReal pullback of Lebesgue measure restricted to [0,t]. Endpoint differences do not change these Lebesgue integrals. The product measure used by ProgressiveL2Integrand is P.prod(TimeMeasure.upTo T), with the process arguments swapped in processFunction.
recursive_binder_and_definition_audit.driver_identity: coordinateFamily(hB i).process j t omega is exactly the j-th coordinate of B i t omega. Both equation blocks pass its same scalar Brownian proof to itoIntegralProcess. The pair must therefore use one Fin d driver, not independent X/Y blocks.
recursive_binder_and_definition_audit.ito_representation: itoIntegralProcess is the existing canonical limit of elementary processes, patched to zero on its null bad set; it is not an unconstrained primitive. Its continuous finite-horizon representative and martingale theorem are available. hEquation supplies the relation of that actual integral to X,Y.
recursive_binder_and_definition_audit.measure_and_filtration: P coerces to the same Measure throughout. The filtration is indexed by NNReal and subordinate to the ambient measurable space. Usual conditions mean completeness at every time and right continuity; finite measure follows from ProbabilityMeasure.
recursive_binder_and_definition_audit.noise_constructor: sphereMeasurableNoiseIntegrand has actual process sqrt(2*lambda)*projectedNoiseColumn j (X_i t omega) k, with the analogous Y expression. The column equals delta_kj-x_j*x_k. Its strong progressivity and L2 property are constructed on the finite horizon. The literal norm bound supplied for the constant temperature is a proved constructor witness, not a bound assumed on the solutions.
recursive_binder_and_definition_audit.real_extension: Real.toNNReal clamps real t to max(t,0). The current endpoint conclusion respects that definition and makes no unsupported two-sided zero-time differentiability claim.
recursive_binder_and_definition_audit.vector_brownian: The current definition requires standard vector Brownian law, strong adaptedness and independence of future vector increments from the past filtration. Standard vector Brownian includes zero at time zero, Gaussian linear projections with elapsed-time covariance and a.e. continuous paths. No independence is asserted between different particle indices.

role: Independent source and candidate-statement reviewer; neither candidate formalizer nor the future blind decoder
scope_boundary: No solution existence, uniqueness, model-wide theorem, density equation or PDE closure is established.
No supplied nonlinear Ito identity, zero-mean certificate or expected differential inequality may replace the original coordinate SDE premise.
No replacement of an actual fourth moment by the square of a second moment is accepted.
Merely measurable/time-dependent temperature, stopped processes and global uniform bounds are outside this fixed-continuous setting.
Any downstream application requires its own explicit interface adapter; this statement review awards no downstream certificate completion.

seven_semantic_slots.assessment: The supplied processes X_i,Y_i take values in the literal Euclidean unit sphere. The target concerns their actual probability expectations. The Brownian family, probability measure, filtration, two configuration-dependent drift fields and fixed temperature are explicit; no abstract energy certificate replaces the processes.

N,d are natural numbers, N>0. State space is EuclideanSpace R (Fin d); configurations are Fin N to sphere. Stochastic times are NNReal. D,R4,L,G are real-time functions obtained using Real.toNNReal, so they are constant on negative times. The sphere and finite configuration space use their induced topological/Borel structures. The dimension is cast to R before subtracting 1 or 3; there is no truncated natural subtraction.

All data are universally supplied in the displayed binder order. For every positive horizon T and its positivity witness, the coordinate equation holds outside one null set simultaneously for all t<=T and all particle/coordinate indices, and for both X and Y. The exceptional set may depend on T. Countably many integer horizons suffice for any later global continuous-path event; an uncountable intersection is not justified.

One probability measure, one usual filtration, each vector Brownian relative to that filtration, joint measurability and strong progressivity of X,Y, continuous full-configuration coefficients and fixed lambda>=0, plus the original linear coordinate integral equations. No interparticle independence, tangency, Lipschitz/global bounds, d>=3, pre-existing path continuity, initial measurability, drift/noise integrability, nonlinear Ito balance, martingale centering or expected derivative is supplied as a new premise. Joint measurability is source-listed but redundant mathematically in this time/state setting; see N1.

D is the normalized sum of actual second moments; R4 is the normalized sum of actual fourth moments; L is twice the normalized sum of expected inner products with bX-bY. G=L-2*lambda*(d-3)*D-lambda*R4. The conclusion gives continuous and locally integrable G, the oriented two-time integral identity, finite-interval absolute continuity, a derivative at every positive time and the right derivative at zero. It asserts no derivative expectation interchange as an assumption.

Coordinate equations are a.e. in samples and simultaneous throughout each positive horizon. The final expectation identities and derivatives are deterministic, not merely a.e. in time. At zero the conclusion is HasDerivWithinAt on Ici 0, not a two-sided derivative of the clamped extension. Global continuity/local integrability of the clamped G follows from its nonnegative-time continuity. The all-a,b oriented identity is an elementary extension of source F1 by antisymmetry; see N2.

N,d and the single fixed lambda are the only explicit numerical parameters. Finite-horizon coefficient bounds may depend on the horizon, fields and finite dimensions; they are derived using compactness and are not uniform-in-time assumptions or exported rate constants. lambda=0 is included. The exact identity needs no d>=3; such a restriction belongs only to a later sign inequality. Every Ito integral for pair i uses precisely coordinate j of B_i with the same measure and filtration.

verdict.explanation: The proposed single result faithfully captures the supplied synchronous coordinate equations and exact expected energy balance, with justified derived strengthenings. Acceptance permits proof implementation under the recorded guardrails. It is not a compiled theorem, blind roundtrip, proof audit or downstream application closure.
